newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds lower, spreads widen modestly.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds lower, spreads widen modestly.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were lower and yield spreads were slightly wider late on Tuesday as few traders found little incentive to buy.
"It was fairly quiet today ... mortgages continued to do well," said one Ginnie trader, referring to yield spreads to Treasuries.
Mortgage spreads have tightened about 10 basis points over the past week, the trader said.
Earlier losses in both Treasury and mortgage-backed paper were exacerbated immediately following a strong consumer confidence report.
The Conference Board reported that consumer confidence in May surged to 127.1, a 28-year high.
But mortgage prices rebounded a bit as market participants digested the report.
In pass-throughs, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent coupons were off 8/32 at 99-04/32, yielding 99 basis points over the 10-ybar Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae was off 7/32 at 99-04/32, and Freddie Mac issues were down 6/32 at 99-11/32.
The five-year note was off 6/32 at 6.62 percent, while the 10-year note was off 9/32 to yield 6.79 percent.
